notes: RPW data: Third Quarter 2025 (collected 8-28 Aug 2025), the most recent quarter listed on the corridor page as of 2026-10-15. Send amounts: EUR 140 (USD 200 basis) and EUR 345 (USD 500 basis). Corridor average 5.48% (fee EUR 5.32, FX margin 1.68%) is the USD 200 average; no USD 500 average was readable. USD 500 rows for WorldRemit, Xoom and the Intesa Sanpaolo branch transfer are missing because the page text was cut off when read, so they are omitted rather than guessed. Poste Italiane (via Western Union and via MoneyGram) and Intesa Sanpaolo (via Western Union) show NEGATIVE FX margins in RPW (the rate was better than the reference rate on the survey day). The Poste/WU total cost is negative (-0.12% / -0.54%). These figures are reproduced as published; consider a footnote. RPW lists 'Internet' as access, so send_method 'online' may cover both web and app. send_method 'post-office' (Poste cash row) is not in the brief's enum. Paysend's receiving method was blank in RPW, so payout is null. firm_type follows RPW (Remitly, WorldRemit, Paysend, Xoom are classed as MTO). Regulators added in a second pass (2026-10-16): WorldRemit Belgium/NBB (WorldRemit T&C), PayPal (Europe)/CSSF for Xoom (Xoom user agreement names the entity; CSSF as its supervisor is mentioned in that document but not stated as the EEA authoriser), Paysend EU DAC/Central Bank of Ireland (entity from Latvian FCMC passport register, CBI EMI licence from Paysend press release, which does not name the entity), Attijariwafa Bank Europe Italian branch/ACPR+Banca d'Italia (third-party bank directory pickthebank.eu, not the regulator's register). Intesa Sanpaolo's licence is general knowledge, not checked against the register this session. Remitly's entity comes from a 2019 news article (fora.ie), not its current terms. For Poste Italiane, PostePay S.p.A. is confirmed as the provider of the MoneyGram service only; the provider entity for the Western Union service (FI_PPWU sheet) was not read. No Tunisian payout partner names are given because no source stated them. Wise: its own EUR to TND page (wise.com/be, Belgium) says recipients get TND from Wise's local bank account, so EUR to TND looks supported. Wise is not surveyed by RPW on this corridor, so there is no offer row; it is not listed under not_available. Confirmed on 2026-10-16 on wise.com/it/send-money/send-money-to-tunisia: EUR to TND from Italy, paid into local bank accounts from Wise's local account. Consider adding Wise as a non-RPW offer using Wise's own pricing. Sources: https://wise.com/be/send-money/send-money-to-tunisia, https://wise.com/it/send-money/send-money-to-tunisia Re-checked 2026-10-16: RPW corridor page still shows Third Quarter 2025 as the latest; the USD 500 tab content for WorldRemit, Xoom and the Intesa branch row is still not readable (only USD 200 figures come back).
